Subject: Recap + model suggestions for MedLytics long-context POC

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have the same plan moving forward.

Key use case we captured:
- Clinical note ingest + timeline summarization for multi-visit patient records (average 15–30k tokens per record, some outliers ~70k).
- Must preserve event ordering and diagnosis fidelity; downstream extractors are sensitive to hallucinated dates/medication names.
- Latency target for real-time UI preview: 2–3s median for 4k token outputs; offline batch can be higher.

Immediate concerns you flagged:
- Truncation behavior and which tokens get dropped when records exceed the context window.
- Summarization fidelity: retaining critical findings and dates.
- Quality regressions when we switch quantized/low-cost variants for scale.

What we recommend for initial POC (short list):
1) Model candidates to try (ranked by fidelity -> cost):
   - rw-ltm-13B-64k: strong long-context attention optimizations, best-in-class for preserving temporal cues on our internal tests.
   - rw-recall-70B-64k: higher base quality for abstractive summaries, good with temperature 0.0–0.2 for determinism.
   - rw-cost-7B-32k-quant: fallback for bulk batch summarization where throughput matters (expect slight loss of nuance).

2) Eval artifacts we’ll deliver:
   - a benchmark CSV with truncation/recall metrics across chunking strategies (attached).
   - a prompt suite to exercise date/med name retention and hallucination checks (prompt_suite_v1.md attached).
   - automated regression harness that compares new model outputs to your golden set with token-level diffs (link below).

3) Short-term plan + owners:
   - Redwood will run the first pass of the long-context evals against your sample dataset (we’ll use the three model candidates above). Owner: Priyom.
   - MedLytics to share a redacted sample of 100 records spanning short/medium/long (>50k tokens) by EOW. Owner: Sam.
   - Joint sync in 10 days to review results and pick the production variant.

Attachments: medlytics_longcontext_eval_summary.csv (CSV), prompt_suite_v1.md (Markdown), POC_scope_and_timelines.pdf (PDF).

Immediate ask: can you send the redacted sample and confirm whether PHI handling requires on-prem/private deployment for the POC? If it does, we’ll provision a Private trial instead of hosted.

Thanks —
Dylan

Hi Sam —

Great questions. Short answers first, details below.

1) Private vs hosted: Private trial will remove any ambiguity for procurement — we can spin up a VPC private plane for the POC. We’ll need a short access/egress matrix from you.

2) Chunking vs full-window:
   - If you can fit full records into the model window (rw-ltm-13B-64k or rw-recall-70B-64k) prefer single-pass full-window inference — it preserves ordering and reduces stitching errors.
   - If some records exceed 64k, we recommend an overlap/stride approach: split into 32–40k windows with 2–4k overlap, generate per-chunk summaries, then run a concise consolidation pass. We include tests in the attached CSV showing that a 3k overlap retains >95% of event mentions for our clinical test set.

3) Quantized 7B regressions:
   - Empirical summary fidelity delta vs 70B on our dataset: F1 (entity retention) drops ~6–9 percentage points; hallucination rate increases modestly for rare medication names.
   - For deterministic parts of the workflow (date extraction, ICD code retention) 7B-quant performs close to the larger models if you use explicit extraction prompts and a higher beam/temperature=0.0 setting.

4) Proposed evals we’ll run for the POC:
   - Truncation recall matrix (attached CSV).
   - Prompt set stress tests: date/drug/name perturbation scenarios (prompt_suite_v1.md).
   - Summarization fidelity report: entity-level diffs and timeline preservation score.

Next steps:
- We’ll provision a private POC tenant unless you confirm hosted is acceptable. Dylan — can you own the tenant request and procurement intro?
- Sam — please send the de-identified dataset. Marissa — I’ll need the eval cluster (small) provisioned for Thu to run the first pass.

Priyom
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
